newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BOE's George says independence not linked to EMU.
newsitem.headline: BOE's George says independence not linked to EMU.

text.p: Bank of England governor Eddie George said on Monday that the decision to make the British central bank independent was not connected to any considerations about Britain's possible participation in Europe's economic and monetary union.

Asked whether the independence of the BOE had anything to do with EMU, George said no. "It is a neutral decision. It's a British solution to a British problem," George told reporters ahead of the month meeting of G10 central bank governors at the Bank for International Settlements.
Last week's decision by Britain's new labour government to give the central bank independence to set interest rates meant that Britain would fulfill one of the conditions for joining EMU.
However, Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has said it is unlikely Britain would be an EMU member in the first wave due to start in 1999.
